items.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: Harry Reser, he played like a violin player would play, you know, those banjo solos.

ctx.x: But did it ever get to the point where all of a sudden your father was saying now wait a minute, this music stuff is okay for fun—

Oh yeah, yeah. Well then after he got me the banjo, then he got me a teacher in a candy store. The guy owned a candy store and I’d go back there and he’d show me. But he did do one thing. I had two banjo teachers. And they at least tried to make you learn how to read music. You know it wasn’t like C or nothing like that, it was written out and you had to learn where everything is. Now they have all the, like Harry Reser’s, he was a popular band leader, Cliquot Eskimos I think they were called. Harry Reser, he…
